items.followUp: How does light intensity affect the rate of photosynthesis?

rubric.why: Recognizes that the rate rises as temperature increases, up to an optimum.
rubric.description: The rate of photosynthesis increases with temperature up to an optimum.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the rate increases with temperature up to an optimum.

rubric.why: Identifies the fall in rate at temperatures above the optimum.
rubric.description: Above the optimum temperature, the rate of photosynthesis decreases.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the rate decreases or falls at high temperatures.

modelAnswer: As temperature rises, the rate of photosynthesis increases up to an optimum temperature.
Above the optimum temperature, the rate decreases because the enzymes involved are denatured.

items.followUp: What is the role of oxygen in aerobic respiration?

rubric.why: Defines the Krebs cycle as a cycle of reactions and identifies its location.
rubric.description: A cyclic series of reactions occurring in the mitochondrial matrix.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing it as a cycle or cyclic series of reactions in the mitochondria.

rubric.why: States that acetyl CoA is oxidised and carbon dioxide is released.
rubric.description: Acetyl CoA is oxidised, releasing carbon dioxide.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that acetyl CoA is oxidised or broken down to release carbon dioxide.

modelAnswer: The Krebs cycle is a cyclic series of reactions that occurs in the mitochondrial matrix.
In it, acetyl coenzyme A is oxidised, releasing carbon dioxide and energy-rich products such as NADH and FADH₂.
